scenario: AITA for telling my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together? | My girlfriend expects me to build a future for us. A little back story: She's a student right now and works part time but barely makes enough to pay her rent/school fees. I'm 24 and work a minimum wage + commission job, I have barely any money saved so she doesn't understand why I spend so much money/time with family We've been dating 3 years with no problems except for this, we love each other and live independent lives but she worries that I'm too focused on helping my family and making them happy instead of building a future for us. She's working as much as she can to pay her bills but because shes a student and also doing her required interning she can't work much more. She doesnt ever ask me for money to help her right now because she wants me to save up. She doesn't have a family like mine so she doesn't understand, my family is close and I really want to take care of them. She says that I'm supposed to be worrying about my own future right now. She says that she doesn't understand because my mom recently received about ~100k for a settlement and bought a house and a new car and I shouldn't be worrying about helping when they seem fine. She is angry that I dont take my life seriously, I've been trying to get my real estate license for a few months now but cant find the time to study because of how demanding my family is, they get really angry/sad when I'm not around for family events and I understand why, we're a close family. I get where shes coming from but I cant drop my family. I told her all of this and she got angry saying that shes not asking me to abandon my family, she just wants to make sure we have a solid foundation before we worry about helping my family. And I cant build a future if I'm always with them. She expects me to start saving up money for a downpayment on a house while she finishes and gets her degree and can start helping as well but I keep telling her my family needs me first. We had a particularly heated fight, the worst we've ever had last night and she said she feels like I'll never care enough about my future and I'm supposed to be building one for myself and her and she can't be with someone like that. She said if I really feel like helping my family comes before my own future than that is my choice but she's going to have no choice but to worry about herself from now on and plan a future where shes her only priority because I make it sound like I don't want to be part of it. Shes stopped mentioning anything about it and is now talking about saving up for a one bedroom apartment and a car for herself (she lives in a basement). She seems so sad but I cant help but feel like shes wrong for even asking me to not help my family. I dont know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family will always come first. AITA for telling her my family and their needs have to come before her and our future together?

But I also want to build a future with you, and I’m committed to doing what I can to make that happen—within reason. If you’re not prioritizing your own financial growth (e.g., getting your real estate license), how can you expect to provide for her later? Her sadness stems from feeling like she’s being pushed aside. It suggests she no longer feels secure in your commitment. This is a crisis in the relationship, and it’s worth asking: *Is this how you want to treat the person you may one day marry?* Even if you believe family comes first, your actions must not drive her away. 4. **Your Family’s Needs vs. Your Own Growth** - If your family’s needs are being met (e.g., your mom’s settlement), it’s worth evaluating whether your time and energy are being misdirected. Are you helping them out of love and duty, or out of guilt or obligation? If it’s the latter, you may need to set boundaries to ensure you’re also growing as an individual and as a partner. --- ### **What You Could Do Moving Forward:** 1. **Acknowledge Her Feelings and Reassess Priorities** - Start by apologizing for dismissing her concerns and for the way the fight was handled. Say something like: *"I love you, and I want us to have a future together. I realize I’ve been so focused on my family that I haven’t been giving you the attention and commitment you deserve. I’m sorry for making you feel like you’re not my priority. Let’s talk about how we can both grow and support each other."* 2. **Set Boundaries with Your Family** - It’s okay to love and support your family, but you don’t have to be available 24/7. Work with your family to set realistic expectations (e.g., *"I’ll be there for major events, but I also need time to focus on my career and our future"*). 3. **Take Concrete Steps for Your Future** - If you’re serious about building a future with her, you need to show progress. This could look like: - Spending 1-2 hours a day studying for your real estate license. - Setting aside a small amount of money each month to save for a down payment. - Having open conversations with your girlfriend about your financial goals and how you’ll support each other. 4. **Prioritize Her Emotional Security** - She needs to feel like you’re investing in her. This could mean: - Planning small, meaningful dates or check-ins. - Encouraging her in her studies and career goals. - Being transparent about your plans for the future (e.g., *"I want us to buy a house together in 2-3 years"*). 5. **Seek God’s Wisdom** - Pray about this situation and ask God to guide you in how to balance your responsibilities. Sometimes, the answer isn’t about choosing between family and your girlfriend, but about finding a way to love both well. --- ### **Final Thoughts:** Your heart is in the right place—you love your family and want to take care of them. However, your actions are causing harm to your relationship, and that’s not aligned with the love and commitment God calls us to. Saying "family always comes first" without addressing your girlfriend’s needs is not just unwise; it’s potentially destructive to your relationship. If you truly want to build a future with her, you’ll need to show her through your actions (not just words) that she is a priority. This might mean adjusting your priorities, setting boundaries with your family, and taking concrete steps to secure your own future so you can secure hers. **In short:** - **AITA?** Yes, in the sense that your current approach is causing harm to your relationship and may not reflect the love and commitment required for a healthy partnership. - **Is there a middle ground?** Absolutely. You can love your family and prioritize your girlfriend’s future by finding balance, setting boundaries, and taking actionable steps toward your shared goals.
